key_insight: A physics-grounded welding digital twin combines thermal simulation, Gaussian-process surrogates and robotic control to screen in-space joining strategies before experimental testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could support adaptive welding control when robot travel speed changes, helping maintain consistent joint geometry.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates predict weld responses.
A simulated UR5 follows an L-shaped seam while proportional control adjusts the power-source setting.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs in repeated five-fold cross-validation; finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1.0–3.0 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity and robotic hardware-in-the-loop tests are needed to assess model fidelity and controller performance.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
